title: docs: contributing guide, PR and issue templates, path labeler
body:
This adds the files a contributor (person or AI agent) meets first: a contributing guide, a pull request template, issue forms, and a workflow that labels pull requests by the area they touch. Everything is written for appbox as it is: `main` is live, so the guide and template put what a merge deploys to machines, and what each change must say about that, up front. Nothing here runs on an enrolled machine or goes into the image.

## What

- **CONTRIBUTING.md:** the short version of `docs/working-on-the-repo.md` (linked, not duplicated): what each kind of change deploys and when, the image-before-ini and daemon-reload rules, ground rules (no proprietary app baked in, open apps never touched, never rewrite `main`, no em dashes), the local checks (shellcheck via podman, `bats tests/unit`, `node --test scripts/tests .claude/hooks/tests`, the `tests/e2e/` image build), DCO sign-off, the risk tiers (no human-merge gate on any tier; Tier 2 needs reviewer-agent review, tests, and a stated machine impact; the owner's brake is the `hold` label), and private security reporting.
- **PR template:** tier and paths touched, machine impact, checks run, safety checklist, sign-off.
- **Issue forms:** the bug form asks for the machine, GPU vendor, the box's image (`podman inspect apps --format '{{.ImageName}}'`), `--show-config` output, the `appbox-update` journal, and the app. The feature form covers adding an app (licence and vendor apt repo) or a behaviour change. `config.yml` turns blank issues off (the API, which automation uses, bypasses forms anyway) and links private security reporting.
- **Labeler:** `.github/labeler.yml` maps paths to `area/image`, `area/host`, `area/ci`, `area/agents`, `docs`, `tests`. The workflow runs on `pull_request_target` with `permissions: {}` at the top and only `contents: read` + `pull-requests: write` on the job, never checks out PR code, and pins `actions/labeler` v7.0.0 by commit SHA.

## Files

`CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/{bug_report,feature_request,config}.yml`, `.github/labeler.yml`, `.github/workflows/labeler.yml`

## Tests

- `actionlint .github/workflows/labeler.yml`: clean.
- `yq -e .` on all five YAML files: parses.
- `grep -rn` for em dashes over every file: none.
- Checked that `node --test scripts/tests .claude/hooks/tests` (the command the guide gives) runs tests from both directories on Node 26.
- Confirmed `bf12e9b0` is the commit the `v7.0.0` tag points at, and that labeler v7 reads its config through the API at the base commit when no checkout exists.

## Notes

- Under `pull_request_target` the workflow and config come from `main`, so this PR will not label itself; labelling starts with the next PR after merge.
- The `area/*`, `docs` and `tests` labels and `hold` do not exist yet. Labeler creates a missing label on first use (default colour, no description), so creating them first is nicer, not required.
- Private vulnerability reporting is currently **disabled** on the repo, so the security links will not work until it is turned on.
- `docs/risk-tiers.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `tests/unit`, `tests/e2e/` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` are referenced but come from other ACMM PRs.

title: Move redhat-actions buildah-build and push-to-registry to v3
body:
Replaces #9 and #10, which only moved the deprecated v2 tag.

- `redhat-actions/buildah-build` v2 -> v3.1.0 (`719e3c4`)
- `redhat-actions/push-to-registry` v2 -> v3.0.0 (`94ade33`)

Both SHAs match their upstream `v3.x` release tags.

Why:
- v2 targets Node 20, which GitHub is retiring, and is now deprecated upstream. v3 runs on Node 24.
- buildah-build v3.1.0 auto-detects rootless native overlayfs and stops forcing fuse-overlayfs, which upstream says fixes silent data corruption and slowdowns on ubuntu-24.04 runners (the runner this workflow uses).
- The other v3 changes are new optional inputs; the inputs this workflow passes are unchanged.

Testing: this PR's CI exercises the build step. The push and sign steps only run on `main`, so `push-to-registry` v3 is first exercised by the post-merge build. If that fails, revert this PR; machines keep the last good image in the meantime.
